utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I understand you have a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Prior to Mr. Alarid continuing his cross-examination I would like to make an observation about the cross-examination so far. I would like to draw Mr. Alarid's attention as well as the Court's to Rule 90(H)(ii). While we have listened to his suggestions that the witness is not worthy of belief we have yet to hear him put his case to the witness as required by Rule 90(H)(ii). I say this now because I do not want Mr. Alarid to complete his cross-examination without complying with this rule. It is not a rule or legal principle that we observe in US jurisdictions so Mr. Alarid may be unfamiliar with it. And 90(H)(ii) states in cross-examination of a witness, who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for cross-examining party, counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears, which is in contradiction of the evidence given by a witness. The Prosecutor versus Brdjanin on 22nd of March 2002, the Trial Chamber issue a decision reaffirming the role that 90(H)(ii) plays in cross-examination, and I have copies of the decision if the Chamber wishes to review it or the Defence counsel; but in paragraph 12 of that decision the Brdjanin Chamber sets forth the underlying rational of the rule. Where the cross-examining party intends to later contradict the testimony of a witness on a fact in issue by introducing further evidence or by suggesting that the witness's testimony can otherwise be explained, the witness should be given the opportunity in cross-examination to comment upon the contradictory version. The Chamber goes on to state in paragraph 13: "The Trial Chamber states without the least hesitation and stresses that Rule -- the Rule 90(H)(2) it was adopted to serve fairness in the conduct of trial and to expedite trial proceedings in this Tribunal. It is indeed a rule of fairness, not only because it serves to enable the witness to comment upon contradictory version but also to give the trier of fact in this case the Trial Chamber the opportunity to more accurately judge the credibility of the contradictory version." Now on the 9th of January 2008, Mr. Alarid filed a document that was entitled, "Milan Lukic's Defence notice under Rule 67(A)(1)(a). While Judge Thelin ruled that this filing did not meets the requirement of 67(A)(1)(a), the filing did set forth at least in vague terms the Defence case. I'm quoting now from paragraph 21(D) of the filing: "On the counts 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the indictment, Drina River, the accused claims that he was not present or even less participate in that incident, but he will present the witness, a Muslim, who was wounded at that very moment, but from Muslims who opened fire from the other side of the Drina River." It would seem to me that Rule 90(H)(ii) therefore requires Mr. Alarid to put to VG-014 the following facts if this filing indeed accurately represents his case: One, that Milan Lukic was not present at the Drina River when the five men were killed; that Milan Lukic did not try to kill VG-014; in addition his Defence asserts that there was another Muslim witness who was wounded at the very same time the attempt was made on VG-014's life. This would require Mr. Alarid to put to the witness that there was, in fact, an 8th Muslim man at the river that day, or in the alternative, that not all of the five men VG-014 said were killed died that day and, in fact, there was another survivor. With respect to the assertion in the submission that the gunfire that killed the men was "from Muslims who opened fire from the other side of the Drina River," it would seem to me that it must be put to this witness that the shooting did not come from behind him as he has testified but came from across the river. From the far bank which the witness has testified he was facing at the time the shooting began. So if his previous filing is indeed an accurate reflection of his case, then I believe it is incumbent upon him under the rules to put this directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have listened to you, Mr. Groome. I'm familiar with the rule. And certainly in the jurisdiction in which I used to practice, it was the practice for cross-examining counsel to put his case, and the language usually used is I put to you so and. If he doesn't do that, what flows from it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's a rhetorical question, it's a rhetorical question. I'm asking what is the consequence if he doesn't do that? I think the consequence will be adverse to his case. In this case, as far as I can see, the Defence is -- you have the wrong man. And in my view, Mr. Alarid has been saying that. He has been saying, "You have the wrong man." The essential issue in the case is identity. And I am not going to delay the trial because the Defence is not putting particular details of what you consider to be their case. That's a matter for them to determine. If they don't do it, then the Trial Chamber can draw particular conclusions from that. And so I don't wish to proceed with this matter any further. I hear what you have said, and I take it into consideration. Mr. Alarid has heard it. As I have said, I believe that he has been putting his defence and putting it quite strongly in my view. I don't really want to hear from you on this, Mr. Alarid. Because I think we need to get on with the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The only thing, Your Honour, with all due respect the only thing I wanted to mention was not anything but I was not part of this case in January 8. That was the brief time that Mr. Sulejic was here. He had only been on a couple of weeks himself. I think by nature the filings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me stop you on that. You keep making this point, Mr. Alarid. Don't make it any more because you are the Defence counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- and it will not avail you or your client for you to say that you were not in the case at the particular point. You are the Defence counsel now and you have responsibility for the case of the accused, Milan Lukic, full responsibility, and I don't want to hear that as an excuse any more. Let us call the witness now and proceed with the case. Will the court deputy inform me as to the time that has been used by the Defence? The Prosecutor spent 2 hours and 12 minutes, and I intend to allow Mr. Alarid the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, the Prosecution spent 2 hours, 12 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, but how much time has Mr. Alarid spent?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Defence so far spent 1 hour 2 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the witness being brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 14, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not on the right channel. I'd like to try and leave off or start where we left off yesterday. Now, just to clarify one point is you claim that Milan left high school after the second grade of it and left to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether he completed the second grade or was this towards the end of the second grade. That I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But regardless, you believe that he only completed two grades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you claim that he went to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't claim. I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you assume this because what, it was a rumour around school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the rumour was that he went to Obrenovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The police academy there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that he lived in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, do you know in Visegrad who was the commander of the police after the Uzice Corps entered Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who the chief of police was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who the captain was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You don't remember the name Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know where Milan was working before he supposedly went to become a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who the president of the SDS was in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go back to the point in time when the Uzice Corps entered after the two-party elections when the Uzice Corps entered the city. Do you remember that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember at what time the Uzice Corps entered the town because at that time, I was in Gorazde. I know that it was approximately in either March or April, but I myself was not present in Visegrad at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's because you left in advance of their arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you returned, this is when all the Muslim homes were vandalised, destroyed or burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you could blame the Uzice Corps as much as anything for the damage and destruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could not directly put the blame on the Uzice Corps because I don't know that. I didn't see who did that. I didn't see who did what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you don't know if it was locals or outsiders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the -- at the point in time that you left, that was because the trust in the army had eroded amongst the Muslim people, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And thousands of Muslims fled Visegrad in advance of the army's arrival, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And yet thousands were captured in the woods outside of Visegrad, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And those thousands were taken to the football stadium and addressed by the captain, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what my parents told me because they too were captured and held at that stadium and they told me that the captain -- a Captain First Class, they thought he was, a man by the name of Jovanovic, had addressed them at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When were you first able to talk to your parents after the address by Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after I returned from Gorazde. The situation had calmed down a bit because the Uzice Corps was already in town. So that one could go and visit one's parents and such. So that immediately upon returning from Gorazde, I paid a visit to my parents who were living in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And to return to them, you had to pass through several check-points, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: These check-points were manned by Serbs, local, as well as army, whom you did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Of the local Serbs, did you consider any of them to be White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that particular point in time, I did not notice these men at those check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What do you mean by "did not notice"? Because I believe yesterday on cross-examination you said you recognised some of the men as local Serbians who you knew by face.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. You're right. That was at the check-point outside Novi or New Hotel where I recognised Oliver Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How was Oliver dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a camouflage uniform with insignia with a kokarde with a two-headed eagle, and I believe I said that of armaments, he had a Heckler.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the two-headed eagle, the kokarde, what significance is that to you and Muslims in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, this emblem, this kokarde, to us Muslims was a symbol of the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is Chetniks a nice word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned on direct examination a word, is it "balija," which is derogatory to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the word "Chetniks" is derogatory towards Serbians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to tell you. Perhaps to the Serbs it is. To us, this is their designation. This is what they call themselves, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, with regards to the two-headed eagle, would it be fair to say that that -- those are White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably. They too wore these -- that insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: These are the same two eagles that are on the Serbian flag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't studied those insignia. I don't know whether there is any other kind besides that one, but they are designed in that same fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you went through -- you were in town for how long after your return until you went into hiding again or at least the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during that month you worked and every day you had to go to work through several check-points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for 30 days, these check-points, you saw that there were local Serbs as well as army manning them, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at none of these check-points did you ever see Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it will be fair to say that you didn't hear anything about Milan Lukic until the issue of Ms. Zukic came up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not that I didn't hear anything. I did hear that he had killed Behija Zukic. That is the very first thing that I heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so based on that, you don't know exactly when he returned home as -- do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before that, all you knew of him was being a quiet boy that didn't fight with Muslims, that you went to school with for a short time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said -- I've told you this already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you were able to finally talk to your parents, how did they describe this meeting of 4.000 Serbians in the football stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the figure of 4.000 Serbs. I know that there were about 1500 Muslims. And how many Serbs there were, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise. That was my fault in the question. Beyond that, what did your parents tell you about what Captain Jovanovic said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something to the effect that now they had entered the city, that it would be safe, that they could go back to their homes and continue with their regular activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did your parents confirm that Commander Jovanovic claimed that he controlled the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that your knowledge of the White Eagles was through rumour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, through rumour, but also from my own seeing them, because I worked near places where they passed, and so I could see them occasionally, and also from the things which they did in those times, at that time; and they were easily recognisable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In terms of the things that they did, you're talking about the things that Muslims talked about that they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were these White Eagles at the check-points that you passed through every day at work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, outside the New Hotel, there were a number of the White Eagles, and I didn't notice any at the other check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you hear rumours of White Eagles being under control of Seselj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you hear rumours of the White Eagles being under the control of Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you didn't hear that Milan Lukic was in control of the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who could have been in control of the White Eagles except that all of them were thus inclined to go and murder people; and who was in control of them, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that when you were at work, Serbian troops, Uzice Corps, were coming every day and taking workers away, Muslim workers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what I said. I didn't say that the Uzice Corps did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who was taking away people from your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably those White Eagles or the paramilitary units that were there, that were in Visegrad at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say instead of saying "probably," that it's just you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it could have been anyone taking these people away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it was the White Eagles or the paramilitary units and I don't even know how many of them were there, then at the time; but I cannot confirm that it was done by the Uzice Corps or the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, during this time period, a lot of Muslims had their cars confiscated or taken from them, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And these automobiles, would it be fair to say you recognised many of them because of the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in respect of one of those cars, I can say that I recognised it because it was the property of Avdija Hodzic, who lived in the Jondja neighbourhood. It was his car, it was a Lada caravan. It was taken, seized then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever see this vehicle again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after a certain period of time, that car was left under the new bridge, which is quite near the place where I worked during that month after I had returned from Gorazde. It had been damaged, and it was left by the road under the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever pass by the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, after I came back from Gorazde, I didn't pass by the police station. There was an occasion once, with my colleague, to go to the police station because my brother was arrested then, my brother who had been beaten up at the police station. Because of that we sent to see what was the situation with him and if he would be released.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember at least generally when it was, between when you returned from Gorazde and left again on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it was towards the middle of that period. I really don't recall that all that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you see confiscated vehicles at the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, during this time, there was a point in time where a JNA reservist came to your home, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That happened actually one day in the evening, around 9.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He had a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and a grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he threatened to blow you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he was drunk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He was a racist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't explain that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would there be any explanation as to why he was treating you this way, other than he was prejudiced against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't comment on that. Probably because he was drunk. That's why he did it. But I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can a drunk man kill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say if he can or cannot. It depends on the person, on the personality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you afraid for your life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And for the lives of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this was by a JNA soldier, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said that he was a reserve officer. I don't know if he was a member of the JNA. He said that he was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: During times of war, don't reservists become regular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They receive the call-up notice, so I don't know if then they are considered as mobilised soldiers or if they are still considered reservists. I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Regardless, would it be fair to say that you believed that the White Eagles you did saw were under the protection of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I said in my statement that it seemed to me, when the Uzice Corps came in, that there would be peace. It was the same army that I had served in and that they would establish peace, that there would be no bloodshed; but later it turned out that in my view the White Eagles were actually under the protection of the Uzice Corps and the JNA army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when the JNA and the Uzice left town, you don't know how far they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the heavy weaponry was transferred to Vardiste and Jagodina. This is a settlement some 11 to 15 kilometres away in the direction of Uzice. There was a military barracks there at Vardiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, to back up a little bit, when you went to the police station to inquire about your brother, who did you talk to at the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know that there were just two military policemen there. They had camouflage uniforms and white cross belts and they just said that they had brought in my brother for interrogation and that they would release him, but I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so as far as you saw, you only saw military personnel at the police station, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, that's all I saw. I don't know. Perhaps there were others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And your brother was beaten at the police station by the military, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, by the military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this was the kind of harassment of Muslims that was going on all over the place at that time, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And despite the issue over the red Passat, you never heard about Milan Lukic being involved with any of this harassment of Muslims at this time, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. Well, I also said yesterday that I had heard from the other citizens that Milan Lukic had also committed a murder or a killing in the Smajic family. This is all I know regarding the Behija Smajic incident. I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And again, you hadn't had any personal contact with Milan Lukic in the town even in passing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you stopped working around May of 1992, end of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the Territorial Defence stayed behind after the JNA left, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What are the Territorial Defence to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, as far as I'm concerned, it's a term for an organisation or a military unit that was established in that territory for the defence of that particular territory. That's how I understand the term "Territorial Defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And as far as you know, these members of the Territorial Defence could have been committing the harassment and violations of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that as far as you know, they could have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't comment on whether the Territorial Defence committed crimes or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But regardless, the JNA left many weapons behind for them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, small arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, during this time, did you know if anyone could leave the city without a written permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that they could, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you get a permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on who needed one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who was issuing the permits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, these White Eagles, do you know where they were stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said in my statement that the command was located in the Bikavac Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You don't know who was at the Bikavac Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean of the -- from the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes -- do you know anyone that was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question. If you're asking about the Territorial Defence or the White Eagles command or if you're thinking about the hotel staff. Can you please be a little more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to know if you knew anyone at the Bikavac Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So of all the people you just mentioned or different groups of people, you knew no one at that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you gave a statement -- you gave a couple statements in this case, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please just remind me a little bit? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, you gave a statement that was typed in English and Serbian and signed and initialed and you gave the statement -- excuse me -- about the 5th of February 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did give the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this is approximately a nine-page statement that you said you reviewed in advance of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just superficially, yes, glanced over it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but you also gave a shorter statement, December 17th, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Perhaps you can just remind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were asked to look at photographs and comment on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what was it about relating to the photographs, if it was people or different neighbourhoods. It's not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to at this moment take a brief break, at least not allocating to my time of cross-examination, so he could read his statement and then maybe that could refresh his recollection. It's a one -- it's less than one page, half a page, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. He's certainly entitled to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May I approach, Your Honour? I have the statement. Or the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Actually, I'm sorry, that's the English version. Here's the Serbian version. He signed the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What about -- do you have copies for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I can give you the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, do you have a copy of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll see if we have extra copies, Your Honour. I think we may have. I believe it's also available in e-court, if I'm not mistaken. Your Honour, I have three copies, for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we could pull it up on the monitor. It's been downloaded in e-court as 2D365. And 2D369 is the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, is there a problem with -- in terms of the protective measures, with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, the witness's name is at the very top of the -- if it could be maybe cropped to the portion -- I don't believe Mr. Alarid needs the first line. And I'm sorry, the bottom, the signature, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That would be correct, Your Honour, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Has the witness had an opportunity to refresh his recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in December of 1998 you described Milan Lukic as having a large birth mark or mole on his right cheek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that is how you remembered him in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note on e-court that I'm looking at on my panel, the witness's name is being shown. Could I ask that it just not be broadcast that we could all look at it in the courtroom, but it's not broadcast out of court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to inform everyone that it's not being broadcast in the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at this time, Your Honour, we would like to introduce this piece of evidence and tender it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that your memory was clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, the Registrar --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Apologies, Exhibit 1D1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that your memory was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we ask it be admitted under seal given the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that your memory was clearer in 1998 than it would be today in 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could say that. I mean, it's been ten years since then, and my recollection was much fresher then than it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be -- I'd ask you to look at Milan Lukic in the courtroom today, and I'd ask the audio video to put Mr. Milan Lukic on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you do that, I'd like the witness to tell us something more about this birth mark. Could you be a little more specific, give us more details about this birth mark that you say was on the right side cheek of Mr. Lukic? How did it appear and how large was it? Did it have a particular colour? That kind of detail.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was just a small kind of growth, greyish in colour. It wasn't very large. It was just a small growth of a greyish colour. It looked like a mole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I said then that it was on the right cheek, on Mr. Lukic's right cheek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at this time I would ask Mr. Lukic to turn to show his right cheek slightly to the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that Mr. Lukic does not have any mole on his right cheek?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he has two on the left side here, on the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's not what you described in your sworn statement, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it would seem like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Would you have that video shown again of Mr. Lukic's face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we can see that there are no moles on the right-hand side but there are some on the left-hand side and I think that in one of my statements, I said that I didn't remember whether it was on the right side or the left side. I think that it's somewhere in the statements, or in one of the statements. You can go through them and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the interesting thing is this, though, is at June 7th, 1992, you claim that Mr. Lukic had painted his face and arms black, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to assume that anyone that did that at that time was maybe attempting to conceal their features?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that painting someone's face black, it would be hard to see any mole of any kind, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not totally concealing the skin tone and everything. It was just a little bit of colour. It wasn't grease paint that would cover everything. Perhaps it could have been just soot that he put on his hand and just dabbed on his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's why in your statement you claim to still be able to see this large mole, despite the soot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there is no mole today on his right cheek, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying it again, that I said in one of my statements, yes, in the statement that I have in front of me, it does say that it's on the right side, but in one of the statements, it says that I don't remember if it was on the right side or the left side. Maybe you can look for that and then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, no doubt, will bring that to your attention in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, regardless, the person you claim to be Milan Lukic you claim had a camouflage uniform, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what time in the afternoon-evening did the supposed Milan Lukic come to your door and knock on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 5.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long was the total detention before you were at the bank of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the point in time that I was taken out of my house, until the moment that I survived at the Drina River bank, and when I stood up to escape, I had a wrist watch, and I looked and it was 7.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And with regards to the time, you claim that you were at many times less than an arm length's away from this man you claim to be Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did anyone in the -- and isn't it true that according to you, no one in this group of people that shot at you were wearing black, other than their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean wearing a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Any black scarves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Any -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Any black scarves with skulls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that in your earlier statement, you said that Mr. Milan Lukic had an impressive and distinct black mole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say that he had a mole. Now, I again claim that in one of my statements, I said that he had it on a part of his face. Whether it was on the right or left part of his face, I don't know. It is in one of the statements. In this statement which is before me, it is actually stated it was on the right cheek.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is the statement in which you say he said that Mr. Lukic had an impressive and distinct black mole? You can't leave it like that. I'd like to see that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and I think at that time this point in time, Your Honour, given the other -- we could just introduce the statement. I don't have my English copy anymore, Judge, of the short one. I don't believe it's in that one. It's in the larger one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the Prosecutor able to assist with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I do have a copy of the -- I only have one copy of the large ore statement but his testimony or his statement shall evidence there was he had a mole on his face, I don't know which side of his face, it was just on the cheek, above the lips, on the side of the nose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I guess I was mistaken, Your Honour. I was passed a note. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it's not part of your case, then, that in an earlier statement, the witness said that Mr. Lukic had an impressive and distinct black mole?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, judge it may have been just a memory of my case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, with regards to the -- who was also taken with you at the June 7th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my house, myself and Amir Kurtalic were taken away. I've already said this before. Namely that he had fled from the village of Kurtalici. Then from the neighbouring street, Meho and Ekrem Dzafic, Hasan Mutapcic and Hasan Kustura and VG-032.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And with you was claimed to be this gentleman named Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what Lukic called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you claim that he was younger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How much younger than 22, 23, 24?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not celebrate his birthdays with him. I don't know how much younger exactly he was. I didn't ask him about his age. I think it will suffice if I just say he was a younger man. I can't say exactly by how many years younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: He was in an SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What colour is an SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dark green colour. One knows what an olive drab colour is. It is the colour worn by the former JNA, by the troops of the former JNA, their uniform colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And should anyone in Bosnia or Serbia confuse the colour of an SMB uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether anyone should confuse it or could confuse it. When I was doing my military service, we all called it the SMB or olive-drab colour, and I don't know of any other designation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how did you know Amir Kurtalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house in which I lived at Bikavac was the property of his sister, who was then living in Sarajevo, so when he left his village of Kurtalici, he came to stay at his sister's house so that we lived there together for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was you and Amir and supposedly Montenegro and the supposed Milan that went and met the grey Yugo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And on the next street, it was a blond, curly haired, thin, 30-year-old soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he was wearing camouflage, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What colour camouflage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a combination of dark green and a light green colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the blue camouflage, what combinations were those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is a combination of navy or dark blue and light blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Any white or grey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember now those uniforms really. I could not give you an answer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the Vilina Vlas Hotel, you claim that there were five people in the Yugo, correct? Let's put it this way: How many people were in the Yugo and how many people were in the Passat before you arrived in the Vilina Vlas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Yugo, there were five people, four men of Muslim ethnicity and a soldier, the soldier that we referred to before with blond, curly hair, and in the Passat there were three men of Muslim ethnicity and Lukic and this allegedly Montenegro -- this person called Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you arrived at the Vilina Vlas, an extra person got there, correct, or joined you, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no persons joined us at Vilina Vlas but we recognised some persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That was Momir Savic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you claim that you knew him from before as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just by sight, nothing personal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: By sight, where would you see him, how often would you see him during your times in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely. He was working in Varda, in Visegrad. I was working in another place so that we saw each other only very infrequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Mitar Vasiljevic, you knew him from the Panos Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how often would you see him supposedly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school that I attended in Visegrad was behind the Panos, so on my way to school and back, I had to pass by Panos. So that's when I saw him. And also when I stayed at the hotel where we had a sort of lottery or Bingo game, and I would go there to play that game and have a drink or two or sometimes also for lunch, and that's how I got to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you saw Mitar Vasiljevic more than you saw Milan Lukic back in high school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not exactly that I saw Mitar more often. Perhaps I saw less of Mitar Vasiljevic then because I was a young lad, and I didn't go to restaurants and such establishments at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You said you passed by the Panos every day while you were in school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would that -- did that mean you saw him almost every day you passed by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would not mean that, because work was in shifts then. There was the first and the second shift. So I could not see him every day because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, back to the blond soldier, you claim that you knew him but didn't know his name. Where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just from passing, I saw him sometimes in passing, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Passing as a local Serbian or passing during the days you were going by check-points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that. Perhaps during peacetime. I can't remember really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, he's either someone you recognised as a local Visegrad citizen or someone you just recognised because you've seen him more than once in the area during the wartime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say whether it was from the time of peace or wartime. I really cannot remember. 16 years have passed and some of the memories have been deleted from my mind. I cannot recall every single detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there was another soldier you knew at the Vilina Vlas Hotel, correct? Approximately 50 years old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was Susnjar. I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, I'm told you have ten minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And during the time that you were with these soldiers, nobody referred to Milan Lukic by title or name, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And no time in your home did anyone refer to Milan Lukic by title or name, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean by refer to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They never called him Milan, Mr. Lukic, or commander, Captain, those kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would that be fair, Mr. 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific? Clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No one deferred to him by a title of rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would be fair to say that that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move forward to the field by the Drina River. When you got out of the Drina, you said you marched towards the Drina in a column and single file, is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We marched in a column, one behind the other, in a single file, yes, one behind the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And with soldiers on either side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side were Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic, and the other two soldiers were on our left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, can you please explain to the Court how six people entered a Yugo, and was it a two-door or a four-door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every Yugo is a two-door vehicle, and how six people got into it, they know that. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you were stopped at the Vilina Vlas and the windows were not obscured to the Passat, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't paying attention then, whether the Passat was visible or not. I was thinking about what was going to happen to us. I was not interested where the Yugo was or what the Passat was like or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the Yugo a small car, a medium-sized car or a large car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yugo is a medium-sized car. It is not of the smallest kind, and it is definitely not of the large kind. It is a medium sized car. It was a five seater at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You were not wearing blindfolds or hoods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What kind of car is a Peglica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Peglica is a small car, it is a smaller car than the Yugo, I think. I saw some Peglicas in town, but I have never driven one or sat in one. I cannot tell you exactly how spacious it is or how many seats it has or things like that. I couldn't explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be difficult to get six people into a Peglica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it would be difficult, yes. Now, whether it could be done, whether someone could or would put six people inside, if he had to, perhaps then it would be possible, maybe even ten people could be put inside; but according to regulations, it is registered for five people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How would you know the regulations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a driver myself. I have to be aware of regulations. I have to know how many people I can drive in my vehicle. I can put four people inside and I can also be inside as the driver as the fifth person. Otherwise I would have to pay a fine. That's why I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's for a Yugo as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, considering the fact that there were two Serbian soldiers in the Yugo and four Muslims, you mean to tell me you didn't hear any kind of discontent about who was going to sit where in this too-small car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I mean, he has said it was medium size. His own evidence in answer to me is that it was a medium-size car. So it's not fair to put to him that it was a small car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour with all due respect to the semantics of medium or small we could produce pictures of Yugos. They are a compact car, at least in my opinion, but of course I'm not giving evidence; and I guess we could produce photos of a Yugo at some point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But his evidence is that it was a medium size car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Fair enough, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But this medium-size car still only took five passengers, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when the shooting began at the Drina River, your positive it was single individual shooting, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And having been in the JNA and training, you know the difference between automatic gunfire and single-shot fire, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a big difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And anyone should be able to tell the difference between that just listening to it; would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that would include at a distance, such as when the Serbs were having gun training on the other side of the forest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you escaped this, you travelled to a village and stayed there for a few days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. You mean when I fled the scene where we were executed and then fled to the villages? If that's what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, if that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very confused, the witness is asking for Mr. Alarid to clarify the question. Now Mr. Alarid is saying, If that's what you understand me to mean, that's what I mean. I think we are getting a bit circular here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, just ask the question, reformulate it, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that when you escaped the attempted execution, you went to a village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you speak with -- did you speak with citizens of this village about the incident that happened at the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the village, I told the people that that incident had happened, that we had been led to that spot, and I took some of the villagers to the place for them to see it. My village was quite near the scene of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The time keeper tells me that your time is up. What -- did you have a few more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just a few, Your Honour, considering that we are at the ends of the sort of the story, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you must be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I will, sir; I will, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 14, when you say you took these people over there, didn't that mean you had to enter sort of enemy territory to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time, my village was not under enemy siege. It was a secure village. There were no troops there, nor were there any individuals there taking people away from the village and similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm not referring to that. I'm referring to the river bank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not take them to the river bank. We looked from a nearby hill. We looked at that spot from the other bank of the river Drina, from a hillock on a meadow which was mine which I used as a local, as a villager. It wasn't on the bank of the river proper that we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How far away was your vantage point when you took these people there to see the river bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is it -- did -- of the people you spoke to in the village, did anyone come to you and say they witnessed this as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I believe that I've already mentioned two of my neighbours who were working in the field quite near the scene of the event but on this other bank of the river, on the other side, on the left bank, and that they heard shooting and they actually took cover in the field because they were thinking someone was shooting at them. I think I have already referred to this as to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, isn't it true that someone from the other bank fired at the position where you were at in defence of your situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the -- who were the -- and I -- could we go into private session for purposes of an asking for a name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I must say your cross-examination has been germane in my view at any rate. Are you at an end?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think so. I would like to opportunity to see the English translation just to make any references if need be and otherwise I'm just about finished. I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The English translation of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The 1994 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It has been provided, Mr. Groome says, so your case manager should have that but can you pass that to Mr. Alarid? We have a very cooperative Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour it was disclosed the 11th of October last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we take the break to allow me to read this, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't want to give the impression that I'm allowing you to prolong this. We'll take the break, and we'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, you have seen the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour, and at this point in time we would have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I have a question for you, though. I notice Mr. Groome is not here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I'm sure he's detained for only a couple of minutes. I would can the Court's indulgence. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't clear to me what the significance was of the questions that you have put to the witness regarding his neighbours witnessing the river incident. What's the relevance? Are you saying that that incident didn't take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm saying it took place in a manner different than this witness described, and I do believe the next witness addresses that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Before -- Mr. Groome are you going to re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. I wanted to ask the witness two questions. Witness, you remember that you have testified that Mr. Lukic was a quiet boy at school, he didn't fight with Muslims, he had occasionally greeted you. Against that background, I want to ask you whether the first time when you heard of his activities in the conflict, and I believe you said that that you heard of some incidents in which he was involved before the killing of Ms. Zukic, were you surprised to hear that being said about Mr. Lukic, the person that you knew at school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I couldn't even believe that something like that could be, that a person could change so much and do such things that are not typical of his behaviour or generally that a person can be kill at all for any reason because he's a Muslim or some other reason, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You said that you couldn't believe something like that could take place, that a person could change so much. So that are you then saying that the activities that you heard of, as being attributed to Mr. Lukic, the conduct that was attributed to him, you found that to be out of character, to be inconsistent with the person that you knew at school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You also told us that the last time before you saw Mr. Lukic in June of 1992 was the year he left school, which was 1984?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When he left school, he would have been 17, and when you saw him again in 1992, he would have been 25 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A person's appearance can change between the age of 17 and 25. Would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a person can change, but they cannot change so much that they would become unrecognisable or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you was whether the Mr. Lukic that you saw in 1992 was the same person physically -- had he put on more weight, for example -- as the person that you last saw in 1984?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, during that time, eight years or so, a person can grow. He was taller, and I said that in my statement, he had brown hair, and he wasn't that much fatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But as compared with 1992, you have said that the person, Mr. Lukic, who is in court today, is fatter than the person that you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Compared to 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. VG-014 I want to clarify a few matters that were raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me just make -- get something clear. Mr. Cepic, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Am I correct in stating that the -- a Chetnik refers to a movement that was very prominent in the Second World War, resistance movement, by Serbs that resisted the Nazi invasion of the territory? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that today, people that are still very loyal to that movement, very proud of their participation in that movement, will, with pride, refer to themselves as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think that they do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just one technical matter. I think it that those questions have a character of leading questions which are not allowed in re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's quite true, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's such a tangential matter. I don't think it required --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I can put it to him then. So is Chetnik a derogatory term? Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand. As far as I'm concerned, yes, it is a derogatory word, Chetnik, balija, yes; but as for how people like to refer to Serbs, well, that's their affair, their problem.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: How people choose to refer to themselves, that's their problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be offensive under any circumstances for someone to refer to a Muslim as a balija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have testified that you had between 300 and 400 students in your year, in the technical school that you and Milan Lukic attended. Did you know every one of those 300 to 400 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I were to give you a pad of paper now and we were to give you approximately an hour or so, how many names do you think you could record of people you attended school, who were in the same year as you and Milan Lukic in school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number that I would be able to recall. I've forgotten some names. Perhaps if I were to read the name then I would remember, yes, that person went to school with me. There were lots of names. Some of those people are still alive. Some are not. Perhaps if you wish to check my ability to do so, I mean, we can do that. I'm willing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not asking that we actually engage in the exercise. I'm just asking you if you're able to approximate how many names do you think you would be able to remember from your school days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 100 to 150 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And out of those 100 to 150 names that you would write, would they be Muslim names, Serb names or a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combination of both, both ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alarid asked you -- I don't have the precise wording of the question, but it was something along the lines that you in the Passat did you not notice some discontent in the Yugo when people were being in his view, too many people were being asked to sit in the car. It seems to me that maybe you haven't made clear the sense among the men that were being detained. Can I ask you to describe the state of -- your state of mind and the state of mind of the other men that were detained at the time you were being forced into the car and taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My feeling was that I had been taken away, I'm going to be beaten up perhaps, mistreated, maybe even killed. These were my thoughts as I was being driven from my house to the Vilina Vlas Hotel and then from Vilina Vlas to the river Drina. My only thought was that I would be executed somewhere or mistreated, abused. This is all the -- these are all the thoughts, the only thoughts, that were going through my mind at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the situation such that you felt that you or the other men could say to Milan Lukic, look, it's too crowded in that car, I'd like a window seat, please don't make me sit in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could gain the assistance of the director, could I ask that we once again zoom in to Mr. Lukic who seems happy enough to show his features, so I'd ask if we could zoom in again once so I could ask if he turn so that we could see the left side of his face. I have my video monitor, I'm not able to see it, if the director would be able to zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to read your statement that -- your first statement. If Mr. Lukic, if you could turn your head the other way so we could see the left side of your face, the other way, please. He had a mole on his face, I don't know on which side of his face, please turn -- if you could look to your right again, Mr. Lukic, he had a mole on his face, I don't know on which side of his face, it was just on the cheek, above the lips, on the side of the nose. Now we can see, Mr. Lukic has what appear to be two moles on the left side of his face. Are they consistent with the moles as you recall them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask Mr. Lukic now to look to the left -- to his left. If you could look towards Mr. Sredoje Lukic. And if we could zoom in just on his cheek, and VG-014, do you see what appears to be a small round scar consistent with a mole having been removed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the scar is visible. It's -- I don't need to explain where it is. I don't know if it could have been removed or if it's a scar from youth. I really couldn't say. But in any case, the scar is very clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just let us remind ourselves, at least I'd like to be reminded where exactly did the witness say the mole was, the one on the right side?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the statement dated the 5th of February, 1998, it was not in evidence, so I was reading simply the line that referred to it. I can simply tender it into evidence if the Court would like the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I it's not an e-court exhibit but I can give the ERN number and perhaps we can send an electronic copy at the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you just read that part, you said something about above the lip.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay I'm quoting from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
