utterances.text: -- page 5 of that statement, the ERN number on this particular page is 00584533: "He had a mole on his face, I don't know on which side of his face. It was just on the cheek, above the lips, on the side of the nose."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we are going to have that in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So Your Honour, if I could tender the statement of VG-014 under seal dated the 5th of February 1998 bearing ERN numbers 00584529 to 00584538, we will forward an electronic copy to the registrar as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And we'll admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will become Exhibit P5 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG-014 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour could I also ask that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: My colleague is saying that we should also have in evidence the shots of his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest that, Your Honour, if it's technically possible, I would ask the director to produce stills of the two sides of the face and the Prosecution would tender those. Perhaps over the next break, I can explore that with the director and then formally tender them once I have the still images.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-014, Mr. Alarid has made numerous assertions that for reasons that you dislike Serbs, for personal vengeance or because of rumour you are falsely accusing Milan Lukic of this crime. Did you come here to The Hague to falsely accuse Mr. Milan Lukic of trying to kill you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll allow it. I don't consider that to be leading. It arises from your cross-examination. It's not leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not come to The Hague to testify because I don't like Serbs or anything like that. I came to testify about a true event that happened to me on the 7th of June 1992. This is a true incident, and I stand behind my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid has spent sometime with you discussing your knowledge of many different crimes perpetrated by local Serbs against the Muslim population of Visegrad. If I were to ask you to list the names of all of the people who you heard, all of the names of local Serbs, who you heard had perpetrated crimes, serious crimes, against Muslims, without telling us the names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I finish the question before there is an objection to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without asking you to tell us any names, can you tell us approximately how long would that list be how many different people do you believe perpetrated crimes against the Muslim population of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the point of that question, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think it will be clear with my next question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is your objection, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour with your leave the same as yours because this is something which was not raised from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it will be very clear how it was raised in cross-examination in my next couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without an answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let me hear what the next question is -- would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have testified that in addition to Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic, taking the men down to the river and shooting them, there were two other men there that you were not able to recognise or identify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have not falsely claimed or attributed the conduct of those two unidentified men to other people who you believe through rumour or other information you have perpetrated crimes against Muslims, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So I can re-ask my initial question: How long would that list be of possible people, if you wanted to attribute falsely accuse them because you believed based on rumours that they were bad people, they had done something terrible to the Muslim population, how long a list would that be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't have a number for such people, but according to what I knew, perhaps -- and I don't want to exaggerate, but it would be about 30 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In fact, in your testimony you refer to two other people being involved in your detention at the Vilina Vlas. They were people by the name of Susnjar and Momir Savic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but to clarify a little bit, they did not take part in the arrests. I saw them at the Vilina Vlas Hotel. They didn't come to get me. I found them at the hotel. I saw them at the hotel, Vilina Vlas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you're not saying that they had anything to do with what happened down at the river, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that your brother was beaten at the police station, in response to a question of Mr. Alarid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've also said that you knew Sredoje Lukic as being a police officer in that police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already have clear answer from the witness who was present -- who were present in police station at that time so -- and we have a clear answer to relation to the Sredoje Lukic in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, let me understand your objection, though. You're saying the question has already been answered? Or that it doesn't arise?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We already have the answer on this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the previous question is -- you have said that your brother was beaten at the police station, and he said yes. Then the next question is you've also said that you knew Sredoje Lukic as being a police officer in that police station. So how has that question been answered?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Firstly, the witness explained who were present in police station in cross-examination related to that incident in police station. In his previous testimony, direct examination, he explained about position of Sredoje Lukic and his knowledge about him. There is nothing which is raised related to Sredoje Lukic from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's a different point. That's the points you should make. That's the point you should make. He is saying that it doesn't arise from cross-examination. I'll consult my colleagues but I'm inclined to agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, what's your position on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can rephrase the question I think it will be very clear and this is nothing I think Mr. Cepic's objections are -- I think he's concerned about something that I certainly don't intend so -- if I could ask the question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-014, you've testified that your brother was beaten in the police station, you've testified that Sredoje Lukic was a police officer in that police station, you have not falsely accused Sredoje Lukic of anything before this Court, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We already have that answer, Your Honour and this is not from cross-examination; it is not raised from cross-examination, Mr. Groome asked about Sredoje Lukic in direct examination, and we have a clear answer in transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, what was raised in cross-examination was that this man is falsely accused Milan Lukic. What I'm establishing here is that although he may have a motive to dislike Sredoje Lukic because his brother was beaten in the very place that he worked, he hasn't come here and falsely accused Sredoje Lukic and that is something that the Chamber should consider in evaluating his credibility with respect to his identification of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But let Mr. Alarid -- Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object from the standpoint of this: One on direct examination and cross-examination, the witness indicated military police with white belts were at the police station. That was the point I elicited on cross-examination. But in addition to that, I think the Prosecution is leading to the point of eliciting self-serving answers relating to his own credibility. I understand the point he's trying to make, I think the question is improper on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We don't consider that a lot turns on this issue but we believe strictly speaking it does arise because the cross-examination raised questions of the prejudice of this witness in relation to other persons. So to that extent we allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So VG-014, if I could just put to you the last part of the question I think remember the first part you haven't falsely accused Milan -- Sredoje Lukic of having anything to do with what happened to you on the 7th, have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no contact whatsoever with Sredoje Lukic, so that I cannot say anything in the sense that he had done anything or that he had done anything to me, so that I'm not accusing him of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just my final couple of questions for you. Is again you said you graduated in 1985, is that correct, from your technical school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that you went back in 2004, I believe you said, to get some papers or certificates; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I needed my diploma as evidence in the company that I had completed secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then you also testified that when you went back after 19 years, you recognised the present director of the school as someone you knew from your school days as a person by the name of Koke, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how we knew him because prior to assuming the post of school principal he was a Professor of physical education.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Any doubt in your mind that it was the same person, Koke, that you knew from your school days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no doubt whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did it take you to recognise this person named Koke, the person you recall from your school days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you see a person that you know, a short time will suffice for one to recognise that person, if you know that person well, and I did know him well because he had been my physical education teacher for three years; so I had no difficulty at all recognising that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then my final question to you is is there any doubt in your mind, and if you have the slightest doubt it's important that you be candid with the Chamber, that the man you've identified in this courtroom as Milan Lukic is the same person who took you down to the Drina on the 7th of June and attempted to kill you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you saying you do have a doubt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-014 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I have no doubt. That is the person who arrested me in my house, took me to the Drina, and attempted to kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness. That concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, Maxine Marcus appearing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, and Ms. Marcus, your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution calls VG-079, who similarly is a protected witness, so maybe the closed session could remain until he enters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. Before you begin, Ms. Marcus, for this witness, the Chamber will allow one hour for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I ask the pseudonym sheet to be passed to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you know, you have been granted protective measures for the purposes of these proceedings; and therefore, you will be referred to by the pseudonym VG-079. Can you confirm that on the paper in front of you you see your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you confirm that you see your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please sign your name to that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to tender the pseudonym sheet into evidence under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours the exhibit will become P6 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can I kindly request that we go into private session for the few introductory questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you give sworn testimony before this Tribunal on the 11th and 12th of September of 2001 in the case against Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review that testimony prior to coming to court today in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This morning, you clarified one point from your prior testimony where you were asked, after the incident that you witnessed, you were asked if you had seen either of the survivors or spoken to either of the survivors after the incident. And in your testimony, you said you hadn't. Would you like to clarify anything about that this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Because I was present when my colleague who was unfortunately killed, he talked to a new one of these lads, and I was present when he talked to him for a very short while, perhaps some five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, I didn't quite understand the question. You said this morning, the witness clarified a point from his prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And then you said, and in your testimony, he is giving testimony here now, for the first time. What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, this witness is a 92 ter witness, as such and he's been granted the status of 92 ter. As such I'm now seeking to confirm his prior testimony which he gave in the Vasiljevic case. He had one clarification which he made in proofing and with that clarification in mind, I will then ask him to confirm that he would give the same answers and then I would seek to admit the prior testimony as part of his 92 ter package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Yes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With that clarification that you just made, if you were to be asked the same questions today, which you were asked when you provided your previous testimony, would you provide the same responses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours the Prosecution seeks to tender 65 ter numbers 135 and 136 into evidence which are the transcripts of this witness's prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours 65 ter 135 will become Exhibit P7, and 136 will be become Exhibit P8.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd like to discuss a few issues in relation to the incident you witnessed to which you previously testified. Can you please tell the Court if you recall the date of that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: It was on the 6th or 7th of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I had set out from the Jelacic house -- from Jelacici to Hamzici to see whether my house had been burned down and to see my mother who, an elderly woman, had remained a loan in the house and in the evening, as I was returning, I could see that that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Precisely where was your observation point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: On the left bank of the Drina. Just below the Hamzici village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe the surroundings where you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Where I was there below the village some 400 to 450 metres, as the crow flies. It wasn't too far. It wasn't exactly near either.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you in a clearing, in a covered area, on a hill, in a field? Can you describe the spot you were sitting, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: It's in a woods, in a copse, a small forest, it was sheltered, it wasn't quite clear, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why were you sitting there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Because as I said a while ago, I was going to see my house, to get my mother, and I was returning with my colleague to where his family was, and so we just stopped there; it just so happened that we were there at that particular time, and we saw it, and we looked on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you watching with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I was watching with the naked eye, and he watched using binoculars, and he saw more of what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where is he today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Unfortunately, he was killed. He is no longer among the living.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you see first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I saw a car being parked at Sase. There was another car that had already been parked there, and then from that spot, we saw some people going towards the Drina, towards a meadow with alfalfa and towards some woods making their way towards the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just as a point of clarification. You said earlier you were on the left bank of the river. Which side did you see this car and these people arrive on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: On the right side of the river, on the right bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall how many people you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Ten or 11 people. We couldn't make out one of them. At least I couldn't. Perhaps my colleague could see him well, but there were certainly ten and the 11th one was hidden by the woods from my vantage point, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe the people you saw walking down to the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I knew Meho Dzafic, and Amir Kurtalic, and when my colleague said that to me, I took the binoculars to ascertain whether it was the two of them, because he said, "Here, these two are going down towards the bank."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In your previous testimony, on page 324, you were asked to describe the group of people that you saw, including the two you've just named. You said, "Some wore uniforms; others had different kinds of clothes." For the purposes of record that is page 324, lines 9 and 10. Could you say how many had uniforms and how many had different kinds of clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: The ones who were forward, we didn't look -- see them that well but they were in normal civilian clothes and footwear and these other ones had black or bluish uniforms on them, those, they were walking behind the first groups, the first group which was making their way towards the Drina; so we couldn't see exactly whether the uniform they wore was black or blackish or bluish, but they were also carrying some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How many armed men did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I saw three armed men.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you personally know any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, I did not; and I couldn't see who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe the weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They were rifles with long barrels. Whether they were machine-guns or semi-automatic rifles or light machine-guns, I couldn't tell from that distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did they all have the same weapons or different weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could see, the weapons were similar, these long barrels namely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the men in the front, who you described as being in civilian clothes, do you recall how many there were of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: There were seven men in front, in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you named two of them who you knew. How did you know those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They are my colleagues and my relatives and we socialised quite a lot, and I easily recognised them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you see precisely after you saw the men walk down to the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: When they came to the Drina, to the bank, three of them stayed, but we didn't see the other ones, if they had stayed in the woods or something; but in any case, they walked into the mud of the water, up to some 30 centimetres depth, and then they opened bursts of fire on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please clarify a little bit? Who did you see walk into the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I saw all of them walk into the water. They walked in a line, one behind the other, then they arranged them one -- to stand at a distance from 20 to 50 centimetres apart, and then when the firing began, people began to fall into the water, and I got very upset and I couldn't watch that any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you watching this with the naked eye or with the binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: With the naked eye, but when they dropped into the water, my colleague gave me the binoculars then and he said to me, "Look what they did."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How far behind the victims would you say the shooters were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Maybe six or seven metres. I was standing far away, some 400 to 500 metres away, so I couldn't estimate the distance; but in any case they were close to them, they were not standing far away.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And which direction were the victims facing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They were facing the Drina. They walked into the lake, and the other people with the weapons were behind them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall how many shooters you personally saw fire their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I saw three open fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall the kinds of shots they fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They were opening bursts of fire at these people. I don't know what kind of bullets they are. They would know that. I didn't look to see the kind of bullets that they were using.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What happened to the victims after the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They remained in the water, and these other guys returned back to the cars, and then two of them turned around later and then they fired one or two bullets at the people in the water; and then they left, they went towards the cars on the road from where they came.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you personally observe that second shooting with the naked eye or with the binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I was looking with the naked eye. I personally saw what was done, as it was being done.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall when they went back to the cars which direction the cars drove off in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They turned around on the road, and they went towards Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: After they drove off, did you have an opportunity to look back at the victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. Walking for a couple of minutes or so, we reached an area where we could see better, and then after four or five minutes, two people stood up from the water and then we were shouting how someone had survived the execution. They went along the right side of the river Drina towards the Usce and then they came to some logs; and they took a log that was about two to two and a half metres long and that was maybe about 20 centimetres thick and they used that to swim across the Drina, and then they walked or set off towards Donja Brstanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you personally see what you've just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours I'd like to go into private session just for the next two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you personally speak with either of the two survivors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but my colleague spoke with them for some four to five minutes when they came out on the other side. I was there, though. They went to look for their family and this colleague of mine knew one of those people, (redacted) and he had left his wife and children somewhere in town so he went off to look for them and that's where we separated and we didn't see each other any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall what this person said, this person whom you've just named?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I don't know. Are you talking about my brother-in-law or this

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, this (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. No. He just said, "I am going home up at Hamzici." That's where he lived. I didn't know who he was. And my brother-in-law said, "I know this person. He's from Hamzici." And then there was this other guy who was a dental technician, I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not clear there. Who said, "I'm going home, up at Hamzici"? Who said that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did he say that to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He -- I was there when this colleague of mine asked him that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just one more point of clarification on that. This person you refer to as your colleague, is that the same as you refer to as your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you speak to (redacted) any more at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, no, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, were either you or your brother-in-law armed on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, we weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there any combat activity of any kind in the vicinity on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, apart from the execution which you witnessed, was there any other shooting in the vicinity on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: After you spoke with the survivors, did you ever return to your observation post to look back across the river at the execution site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. We went back two days later. The corpses were in the water where they had been shot. After two days, probably the water level was raised from the power station at Visegrad, so probably the corpses were carried away by the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So how many days would you estimate that the bodies were lying there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: About four days, in our estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is that the only time that you saw bodies along the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No. I saw another corpse, that of Nadaski [phoen] and a small child. We saw the bodies of a woman and a child, on some kind of board, and they were dead, and they were going down the river; but we couldn't get close so that we would be able to pull them out and get them out of the water.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, will you be cross-examining this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will you be cross-examining this witness, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 79, you indicated that you were present with your brother-in-law at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he's dead now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what were the circumstances of his death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: He was killed by a shell that dropped in Medja.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: In 1992, in October or November. I don't remember the exact month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you had an opportunity to cooperate with the Office of the Prosecution in around 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when were you first approached by investigators related to these cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Sometime in 2001, maybe January or February.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true you gave a statement the 19th of January 1991 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where was that statement given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you gave the statement under oath to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it documents in its entirety what you witnessed at the bank of the Drina River from your vantage point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, I misspoke. Was the statement given 19th of January 2001? The transcript read 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then you testified in the Vasiljevic case in approximately September, mid-September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was your memory better at the beginning of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe there is a mike open on the Bench. I don't think you intended to have that conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I went just like I did the other time, and I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in your statement of January 2001, you indicated that you were arrested on April 17th, 1992, by the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you were interrogated, and your home was violated and searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: When I returned from the SUP, I met a soldier from the Uzice Corps, and he searched my apartment, the house where I lived, to check for weapons. He didn't find anything. He sat down for a while. And then he left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, last day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason you stopped working is because you received a phone call that three men had come to your home looking for you, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: These three men were wearing hoods, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. Some kind of hood. I don't know. The wife didn't know anyone of them, but in any case they asked for me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so the recollection of the three men coming to your home was through your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And she indicated that they arrived in a red Passat that had originally belonged to Behija Zukic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you stated in your statement that you believed that one of those men must have been Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: It's possible, because he said that he drove it. I -- it's possible. I mean, I didn't know Milan Lukic before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You indicated he said he drove it. Who is "he"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are still in private session, let us move to public session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Milan Lukic he told you he drove a red Passat?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody told him, when he killed Behija Zukic and her husband and her son, he took the car. So there was talk that Lukic was driving around in that car. I didn't know Lukic. My wife didn't know him either. But there was talk that he had killed this woman, the children and the husband, and that he took the red Passat and that he was driving it around. This is the story that was going around. This is what my wife told me, that it was possible that it was him in the red Passat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that this story about who killed Behija Zukic was accepted as true amongst the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They probably did accept that. I don't know if anybody saw him killing them or who knows what, but I mean, it's something that was being talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so when your wife told you the three men arrived in Ms. Zukic's Passat, instantly the name of Milan Lukic was associated with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Probably it was associated with it. Everybody was saying that he was driving this Passat around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, on the 3rd of June 1992, the Passat returned to your home, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you again received the information through your wife that it was the same three men wearing hoods obscuring their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was Mitar Vasiljevic in a hat, in a Volkswagen belonging to Himzo Demir, and there was a woman there with long blond hair, and they went towards another house opposite from my house and then my wife said, "Well, they are coming out, they are coming. Run and hide." So I went and I hid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you certain that you're not confusing the identification of Mitar Vasiljevic and the blond lady with a day different from June 3rd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I don't think I'm confusing anything. That's more or less it, that they were there and that they left, that they took away one person from Gorazde who was turned back from the border at Vardiste and he had a friend there in the neighbourhood; they took that man to Banja and then they brought them back to the house, and they took their Lada away, who took it away, I don't know; but in any case, they brought the man back, and he's still alive to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it would be fair to say, though, that that did not happen on the day of the 3rd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I think that it was around that time, during those days, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in your statement of -- that you indicated that you saw Mitar Vasiljevic with the woman with the long blond hair in Mr. Demir's car in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I didn't see Himzo Demir, only his car, and when there were two things hanging from the side -- from the mirror, from the rear view mirror. Only my wife said something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No. What's more important to me is when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic in the -- Mr. Demir's car, and isn't it true that was May 1992, according to your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yeah, this was in late May, early June, around that time. I cannot remember the precise dates. A person cannot remember everything. So much time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you consider that Mitar Vasiljevic killed Mr. Demir simply because he was driving in her car -- his car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So the only reason Milan Lukic was implicated in this Passat is because people were talking about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were stories going around that he was driving it and no one else. I mean, I don't know what to say. I didn't know Milan before, and I don't know him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Nor did you speak with a direct witness to the crime involving the Passat and Ms. Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you did know this Passat, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long had you seen it around town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Before the war, we knew where this woman worked, where she went in her car, everybody said how good a car she had. This was -- these were the stories before the war. Later, when they said that Lukic had done that, killed her and seized the Passat, I don't know what became of the Passat after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, we are going to take a break now. How much longer do you plan to be? You don't have to utilise the hour that I gave you. It's a maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Actually, I don't think -- can the Court tell me how many -- how much time I've had?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The deputy?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 30 minutes, Your Honours -- [microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Nine minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Nine? Oh, 30. I don't belive I'll take the full hour, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 79, isn't it true that you drew a sketch, if you will, when you gave your statement back in January of 199 -- or excuse me, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it demonstrated how the gentlemen that had exited the cars had crossed the field to the river Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we please have the court usher put on the screen ERN number 01099516?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I just request that that not be broadcast outside because it has the witness's signature on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's to be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: 01099516. For the Court usher's benefit it may be attached to the statements that is otherwise marked as 2D00-0090, which is the English version and 2D00-0084, which is the B/C/S translation or statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If I can assist, it's Prosecution -- oh, you have it up there, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. 79, can you see that drawing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would tender as exhibits, both 2D00-0084 and 2D00-0090 for Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this will become Exhibit 1D2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, Mr. 79, in your original statement, you indicated that the victims walked across the field towards the Drina side by side in a line, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, side by side, in a line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just today, you indicated that they were in single file.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I may have made a mistake, but I stand by what I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So for anyone looking across the river, either with binoculars or without binoculars, it was unmistakable that they were in a line across the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But it is a great distance. It was a great distance, after all. There was a column, they were walking side by side towards the river, and when they reached the bank, they were separated from one another. But they descended in a group, one after another, or two -- in twos and threes, but this is what I drew is when they had already reached the bank and as they were -- when they were separated and when they were already stepping into the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your original statement, you time and time again indicated that there were only ten men, seven being the victims and three being the assailants, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. And there was another, a fourth person, in respect of whom I wasn't sure who or what that person was, but I am certain that there were ten persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that fourth person was a member of the assailing party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Probably. The survivors know that and they will be able to prove that in this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that that fourth person ended up being identified as Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, how this witness knows who the fourth person, he's saying there is three people there. He's saying he has no knowledge about the fourth person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in your original statement, you said you had the binoculars with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: My colleague had the binoculars and then he gave it to me so that I could also take a look, but he used it for a longer time than I did; and I only took a short look because I could not bear to look at what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, during the time that you had the binoculars you were able to identify two of the victims as people you knew, namely Amir Kurtalic and Meho Dzafic, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that was through the assistance of binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. With the aid of binoculars, I actually took it to see whether it was precisely them, and after I had ascertained that I gave them back to my colleague because I didn't have the courage to look on any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And through those binoculars, you were also able to identify the -- what the people were wearing, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: No. I was not. They were in some house wear, slippers, actually I didn't pay any attention to what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that you identified the three men as being dressed in black uniforms, in the original statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. They were black or bluish. It was a distance. One couldn't distinguish between the colours, but they were some sort of uniforms of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you indicated that they had black scarves with skulls printed on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so there was no mistaking the black scarves with skulls in the binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yeah, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of January 2001, you indicated that the originally the men had drove up in two cars, one being a Yugo and one being a Peglica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yeah, Yugo, I call a Yugo a Peglica, how shall I put it? The other one could not be seen. It was parked behind the hedge behind the bushes, how shall I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know what a Peglica is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Well, yes, Yugo and Peglica it is one and the same car or these are similar cars. I wasn't actually paying real attention to see precisely what kind of a car it was. That is what I said in my statement, in fact, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that even in your testimony before the Tribunal on September 12th, 2001, you again referred to the vehicle as a Peglica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. I did refer to it as a Peglica because Peglica is for both driving people and ironing out people, because Peglica is an iron.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in fact your direct answer before the Tribunal was, "There was a little Peglica car, mauve, and also a Yugo, olive green, something like that."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring to this other car which was parked opposite that spot. It was also white and parked behind the woods, but actually it was a car that was damaged and out of order, and it was parked there. I only saw it two days later when I came to that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying there was also -- that the Peglica was also a white car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Ms. Marcus? A point?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, learned counsel has read only up to halfway through that sentence in the testimony, that's not the end of the isn't. This prior testimony page 323, lines 5 through 7, it says, "There was a little Peglica car, mauve and also a Yugo, olive green, something like that because we did not really pay attention to the cars we were looking at these people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just assumed because the statements were admitted under 92, that the Court would of course have the benefit of the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes but she is saying -- what she is saying is you should put this into its entire context to be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So, regardless, you definitely paid attention to the colour of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true the first time you've ever mentioned the colour blue with relation to these uniforms is today in court in 2008?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, it is either black or blue or bluish, that uniform, because from that distance, I couldn't really see, and then my colleague watched for a longer time. As I've said, these were their uniforms which were either black or bluish.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the Court please place on to the witness's screen 65 ter number 164, without markings? It was otherwise marked as Exhibit P3 for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photograph on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Where is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: It is from the cooperative in Sase and up to the place where the crime happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that the willows against the bank have overgrown in this photo compared to 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes. That is so. They were not as tall at that time, and it is only normal that all this growth should have developed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could the court usher instruct the witness on how to use the marking pen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: This here is Sase. This is the cooperative. [Marks]. This is the road to Visegradska Banja. This is the road by the Drina which goes all the way to Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And put approximate location the cars had parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: The cars were parked -- this is the road, this is the house, was somewhere around this place here, down this field. [Marks]. On the road, behind the woods there, that is where they were parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you put a P where the mauve car was, and could you put a Y where the Yugo was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: [Marks]. The car was somewhere around this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: And the other ones, these others were parked somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And for reference, can you put a letter Y by the Yugo, and a letter P by the mauve car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would ask that this be marked as a Defence Exhibit and entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm unable to discern the difference in the cars, the markings, the P and the Y.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks] Y and P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. That's fine now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1D3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, again through your binoculars you were able to identify Amir and Meho, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in your original statement you indicated that the men, the victims, were -- entered the water up to knee high?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so they were not on the sandy bank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They walked into the silt and the water had covered the silt, and they had walked into this silt in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Until they were covered up to their knees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: They came to the bank, and they forced them to walk into the water, and they were -- remained behind them. They were facing the river and their backs were to the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And through your binoculars, you were able to see smoke coming out of three of the machine-guns, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Well, when you fire the shots, it's very difficult to see smoke from a distance of 500 to 600 metres. It's difficult to see smoke. But naturally you can hear the actual gun shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in your original statement you indicated that the assailants had all shot in a burst of fire and not in single shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, there were bursts of fire and then when they were finished, in a few seconds, then they turned to go towards the cars, then two turned back and fired one or two single shots and then they left in their cars; and they turned the cars around and left towards Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And by bursts of fire, you mean automatic weapon fire, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that is unmistakable compared to single shots, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, one of the most interesting things is that at the beginning of your statements you indicate you witnessed this at 11 a.m. in the morning, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Not in the morning. It was in the afternoon sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we please again place D2 in B/C/S for the witness to refresh his recollection? 1D2, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, don't be under any misapprehension. For this witness I will not allow you even a minute longer than the time allotted. The first witness was in a different category. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry, I just want to be sure we are not broadcasting the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we go to the actual statement itself and in the English version the time I'm referencing is in paragraph 6 -- 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, have you read the first sentence of paragraph 7 of your Serbian statement or language -- Serbian-language statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: I don't see where I'm supposed to be reading from. I probably read it before. Whatever I said before and now I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph on the page, the paragraph at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you referring to the line --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The first line of paragraph 7, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "While we were in Jelacici around the 6th or 7th June 1992, at about 1100 hours, a.m." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At around 11.00, I went and I looked at my house in order to go and get my mother, and this happened in the afternoon hours. This is a mistake when this was being typed. At 11.00 I had left Jelacici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He says it's a mistake. That's the explanation he has given.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You had read this statement before you had signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Most probably, but I didn't quite get this 11.00 part. I didn't understand that but I would say it's a mistake. Yes, I did leave Jelacici at 11.00 and I was watching the Drina and so on, and when I returned from Hamzici I was looking at what was happened or what was happening at -- in the afternoon, sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in your statement, you indicated that you talked to the two surviving witnesses or victims of this incident about four or five days after the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: The first time when they came out of the water, I talked with them, and then after four or five days, we looked for them; we wanted to find them to see how they were feeling, because then they left following their own fate, looking for their family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you told them you saw the whole thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Didn't understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You told them you saw the entire incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was there with my colleague who was asking them that first time, as soon as they came out of the water, and then we went our separate ways and we told them that we had seen the whole event, what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you tell the difference between automatic gunfire and single gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, I do -- I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you heard automatic gunfire from across the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now Your Honour, I would like to show the witness a couple of photographs. We've provided them in black and white, but they are in colour for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. -- we are wondering where you're going with this line of questioning. I'd asked you before whether you are disputing that the event took place and you were saying -- you said no, you are disputing the manner in which the Prosecution's alleging that it took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Not just the manner but the circumstances including the identification of the individuals, the vehicles, the manner in which they walked, approached the water, and the number of individuals present. Since considering the fact that the witness and multiple occasions has used the term Peglica to describe the vehicle that approached and the men got out of, I'm -- I believe I'm showing the Court and the witness a photograph of a similar vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And how will that impact on the question of guilt or innocence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, to a certain degree, it seems like the witnesses have the common bond to describe a red Passat as associating with Mr. Milan Lukic. However, if the red Passat was not even involved period in this incident then that brings into further question the veracity or credibility of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your time will be up at half past, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the type of vehicle that is in the car -- or in the photo, I mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: This, the Peglica, or the Yugo? For me it's the same thing. I refer to as a Peglica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the -- the white car behind it, is in fact a Yugo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the car in front is a small Polish car that's considered or at least known as a Peglica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And otherwise would it be fair to say that you just lumped them together because they are both very small cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Because they are small cars and they were far away, and you couldn't see everything, and I didn't look through the binoculars myself. My colleague was looking through them. He hadn't -- he is not among the living. If he were he could have told you about it. So these photographs are not from the place where the incident happened. This is from around town. This is not how it was then. This is something that was taken around town, and you have lots of such examples there, from where you took the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Simply, though, sir, would it be fair to say that this is an accurate depiction of a red Peglica and a white Yugo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now it's clear because I have it very clearly in front of me, and I can see clearly what's what.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you please put the second photograph on the ELMO for the witness, please? Do you recognise this type of car?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what the witness said. Could he please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I recognise it. It's a Passat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that Ms. Zukic had the only red Passat in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: It wasn't as red like that. It was more of a Burgundy. It wasn't like this, not this red. I don't know where this photograph comes from, but if you were going to use a photograph, you should have made a photograph of a Passat in that colour that we were talking about. This is not that colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm showing you a third photograph. Is this closer to the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-079
utterances.text: Yes, the colour is more like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to intrude on the court's domain, but I think the record here if we look back at this record when we return after the break, we won't know which photograph is being shown. Can it be marked for identification somehow? It may be important to show these to other witnesses. Right now all the record shows is that this photograph is being put on the ELMO with no other identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, let us be told what is it that you intend to do with these photographs. Are you seeking to have them admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Your Honour. I think it would be just easiest to benefit the court, the record so you could review at a later date or through other witnesses that we just mark them in the order that they were presented to the witness to avoid confusion, and we enter them as Defence exhibits. We just couldn't get them into the electronic discovery this morning. We were trying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I asked the court deputy to give them exhibit numbers, and she will do that later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, they will become 1D4 and 1D5 respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I might raise an objection to this. We only received them minutes ago, so we didn't receive them when we should have at the beginning of the cross-examination. But I also must wonder, if again thinking about 90(H)(ii) if it's the Defence case that there is a mistake about the Passat, why wasn't this photograph shown to VG-014 when he was here? He's the man who was in the car, not someone who was 500 to 600 metres looking with the naked eye across the river. So I'm just querying why wasn't this photograph, if it's -- if it's important to the case, not put to VG-014?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a point for you to make in your submissions later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only thing I would take exception to with that, Your Honour is simply that I believe in his statement, the witness 79 has been more than clear that he looked through the binoculars so the reference to naked eye I think is somewhat misleading to the record. And at this time, Your Honour, I would tender the exhibits, and I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Marcus, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, if several people were firing at the same time, is it possible that that gunfire could sound like automatic gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours -- I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I uphold the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, that concludes your evidence, Witness. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I believe that will conclude our work for this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there are no more witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are going to resume on Wednesday, the 20th of August at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I address the Chamber on a few matters including the schedule?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: First the stills that were taken today of Mr. Milan Lukic's left and right face I'd ask that they now be formerly tendered, the ERN number of the left profile is 0635-9003. And the profile -- his right profile is 0635-9004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please give them exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, they will become P9 and P10 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would also be helpful to the Prosecution in scheduling witnesses if the Chamber could guide us on the -- is there a formula that the Chamber will use to calculate the amount of time for cross-examination for 92 ter witnesses that will better help us better able to schedule the witnesses if we could calculate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will inform you of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. The third thing is it's been my practice in other cases on the pseudonym sheet also include locations and other identifying information such as the workplace. So the pseudonym sheet would make, include home village with the name of the home village or workplace with the name of the workplace. If that practice is suitable to the Chamber, I will institute it in this case, and it would require us going into private session less frequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For my part, I believe the pseudonym sheet as presented today is adequate. I don't know that we need additional information, but I'll consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We prefer to have it as lean as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And Your Honour with respect to the schedule matter could I ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of August, 2008. 24 25
